csBody.message: Encrypted, then kept in Chrome Sync, which, while sync is on, carries it to your other computers signed in to the same Google account. On a new computer, your master password brings it back. Free, with no extra sign-in.

csBodyOther.message: Encrypted, then kept in browser sync. On a new computer, your master password brings it back, if this browser syncs it there. Free, with no extra sign-in.

csCost.message: It opens with your master password or recovery key. Anyone who gets into your Google account could try to guess your master password; the harder it is to guess, the safer the backup.

csCostOther.message: It opens with your master password or recovery key. Anyone who gets into the account this browser syncs to could try to guess your master password; the harder it is to guess, the safer the backup.

csCostRecovery.message: Only your recovery key opens it, so someone in your Google account has no password to guess.

csCostRecoveryOther.message: Only your recovery key opens it, so someone in the account this browser syncs to has no password to guess.

csSwitch.message: Only the recovery key opens the backup in Chrome Sync

csShared.message: This browser profile isn't yours alone: the backup would go to the Google account this Chrome is signed in to, which may not be yours.

csSharedOther.message: This browser profile isn't yours alone: the backup would go to the account this browser is signed in to, which may not be yours.

csHonest.message: Chrome uploads it only while it is signed in to a Google account with sync on, extensions included. Sixkey can confirm it handed the backup to Chrome, but can't see whether Chrome uploaded it.

csBrowserUnknown.message: Sixkey can't tell whether this browser's sync carries an extension's data: on a new computer this backup may not be there. Also save an encrypted backup file.

csSeen.message: This computer has received another computer's backup, so Chrome Sync has carried one here.

csEmpty.message: No accounts yet: once you add one, it's handed to Chrome Sync automatically.

csWaiting.message: Changes not handed over yet · Sixkey does it shortly

csFailed.message: Not handed over: $1 · Sixkey will try again

csErrBusy.message: too many writes; Chrome Sync takes no more for now

csStale.message: Not handed to Chrome Sync for $1 days: $2

csStaleQuiet.message: Not handed to Chrome Sync for $1 days

csTooLarge.message: The vault is more than Chrome Sync can hold (about 100 KB), so this computer's backup stopped. Sixkey works as usual; save an encrypted backup file below instead.

csNoRoom.message: Other Sixkey backups fill Chrome Sync's space ($1 of them, about $2 KB), so this computer's backup doesn't fit and stopped. Sixkey works as usual.

csHeld.message: This computer's data came from an earlier copy, and Chrome Sync may hold a newer one. The backup continues after a merge.

csNoPassword.message: Set a master password to back up to Chrome Sync.

csUnreadable.message: The data on this computer can't be read, so the backup stopped.

csUnsafeArea.message: This browser doesn't let Sixkey protect its sync storage from scripts in web pages, so Sixkey doesn't back up here.

csUsage.message: Using $1% of Chrome Sync's space (about $2 KB of 100 KB)

csNearFull.message: Chrome Sync's space is nearly full: room for about $1 more account(s).

csOffHint.message: Turning off removes this computer's backup from Chrome Sync; other computers' stay.

csOffHeld.message: Turning off now keeps this computer's backup in Chrome Sync: it may be newer than the data here.

csMergeClean.message: Merge them into this computer and remove them

csMergeCleanHint.message: They're opened with the master password or recovery key you type and merged first, then removed from Chrome Sync; any that don't open stay, and none is removed if this computer's backup still wouldn't fit after the merge. A computer still in use saves its own again.

csOthers.message: Chrome Sync also holds $1 backup(s) of another vault.

csKept.message: $1 backup(s) stayed: they didn't open, or changed meanwhile.

csNotRemoved.message: This computer's backup still wouldn't fit in Chrome Sync after the merge, so none was removed. Save an encrypted backup instead.

csDropHint.message: Only the backups just merged, and not changed since, are removed. A computer still in use saves its own again.

csNothing.message: Nothing in Chrome Sync to merge now.

csMergeAgain.message: The merge didn't finish. Try again.

csFrBox.message: Back up automatically to Chrome Sync (recommended)

csFrHint.message: You can turn it off later in Settings › Accounts › Backup.

csFoundAt.message: Found a Sixkey backup in Chrome Sync (latest $1).

csArrived.message: A Sixkey backup just arrived through Chrome Sync.

csLooking.message: Looking for backups in Chrome Sync…

csFound.message: Backups found: $1. Type your master password or recovery key to open them.

csReadFailed.message: Chrome Sync couldn't be read just now. Sixkey reads it again when it changes.

csNone.message: No Sixkey backup in Chrome Sync yet. If your other computer had Chrome Sync on, it may still be on its way; it shows here when it arrives.

csPartialOnly.message: The backup hasn't fully arrived yet. This goes on by itself once Chrome finishes.

csPartial.message: $1 backup(s) hadn't fully arrived and weren't used.

csWrong.message: That doesn't open these backups. Check your master password or recovery key.

csKeyTypo.message: That looks like a recovery key, but part of it is mistyped. Check it again.

csAfter.message: This computer goes on backing up to Chrome Sync, continuing the copy it was restored from.

csBackupOn.message: Automatic backup to Chrome Sync is on.

csNewCopy.message: This computer's backup starts as a new copy; the one you restored from stays in Chrome Sync.

csFile.message: A copy of Sixkey's automatic backup. Type your master password or recovery key to open it.

csWrongFile.message: That doesn't open this backup. Check your master password or recovery key.

csNeedPassword.message: Opened with your recovery key: set a new master password next.

csOutdated.message: The master password on another computer is newer than the one you typed. You can set a new one now, and change that computer's to it too.

csOutdatedKey.message: The recovery key you typed was replaced on another computer. Use the new one here too.

csOlderKeys.message: Another backup uses an older encryption key; replace the key on that computer too.

csOtherSecret.message: $1 backup(s) don't open with what you typed.

csDamaged.message: $1 backup(s) are damaged or from a newer Sixkey and were not opened.

csKeepPasswordLine.message: Opened with your recovery key. Keep using the same master password as on your other computers, or set a new one if you've forgotten it.

csOrNewPassword.message: Or set a new master password
